translation: Even by the teachers, those two — Sadyojyotis and Bṛhaspati — are to be revered.
Regarding enjoyment and liberation, I will expound the Mokṣakārikā briefly.
(Śiva is) with parts, without parts, endless, effecting action immediately after his own will.

sanskrit: bhogināṃ bhuktaye viśvaṃ vicitraṃ kurute śivaḥ || 2 ||
translation: For the enjoyment of the enjoyers, Śiva makes the world variegated.

sanskrit: sarvasya vedakaḥ || iti | ata eva viśvavyatirekeṇānyasyābhāvāt sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca
translation: (He is) the knower of everything. Thus, precisely because nothing other than the world exists, (he is) omniscient and the doer of everything.
Because (his) activity (is) everywhere, (he is) endowed with that nature, established by valid cognition — thus.
Just as the variegated world (arises) from a variegated seed, so — not from Śaṅkara.

sanskrit: jagadvidhāturmāyākhyasya gamakatvameva | na kāryamupādānakāraṇaṃ vyabhicarati yataḥ ||
translation: Of the world-maker called Māyā, (the world) is merely an indicator; for an effect does not deviate from its material cause.
The material cause that is seen, named 'thread', is insentient.
Having set aside the knowledge and action of Maheśa, (he is) not the cause.
There is no inconclusiveness (i.e., the charge of the reason's being anaikāntika does not hold).
And the result (comes) from the action of persons — what (need) here of the Lord's agency?
Action itself, like actions such as plowing, is accepted as producing the effect — what else (need) be inferred?
But, like plowing etc., (action) depends on an agent possessed of intelligence.

sanskrit: siddhasādhyatā | tatra dṛṣṭe sati nādṛṣṭakalpanā yukteti || 7 ||
translation: (The reason has the required) established-and-to-be-established (character). There, when the seen is available, postulating the unseen is not proper — thus.

sanskrit: pumbhireva bhaved bījaṃ kiṃ hareṇeti tannahi || 8 ||
translation: 'The seed would be from men alone — what (need) of Hara?' — that is not so.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭahānyadṛṣṭaparikalpanābhyāṃ na kartrantarasiddhiḥ | tannahīti tanna yuktamityarthaḥ || 8
translation: By (the two faults of) abandoning the seen and imagining the unseen, no other agent is established. 'Tan na hi' — the meaning is 'that is not proper.'
Then, for the effect beginning with kalā, perpetual origination would be entailed.
Because there is only a relation (and no agent): if the production of effects beginning with kalā (by the non-agent) were to occur, the consequence of no liberation would follow.

sanskrit: yena nākasmikaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kvacana kiñcana || 10 ||
translation: By which (reason) no effect anywhere is seen to be causeless — nor anything (at all).
By which (reason) it was said that an effect without an agent does not occur.

sanskrit: jñānābhāvād bhohyabhoktṛsaṃbandhe na kartṛkatā, kintu saṃbandhamātra iti ||
translation: Because of the absence of cognition, in the relation of the enjoyable and the enjoyer there is no agency — only relation, thus.

sanskrit: tasmād yoge viyoge vā maheśaḥ kāraṇaṃ tayoḥ || 11 ||
translation: Therefore, whether in connection or in disconnection, Maheśa is the cause of the two.
(It is) the Supreme Lord alone, not another.

sanskrit: svabhāva eva vaktavyo gatvā dūramapi tvayā || 12 ||
translation: You must state (it as) own-nature itself, even going far (in your search).
'Much unseen would have to be imagined (and) will come to be' — thus.
(The effect arises through) the activity of one impelled by another, or of an independent one — (so say) the wise.

sanskrit: acetanasya kartṛtvapakṣe na pramāṇamastīti sādhitaṃ pūrvameva ||
translation: In the case of the insentient's agency there is no valid cognition (supporting it) — this was established already before.
Since the independent one is the maker of the effect — an insentient material cause is nowhere (such).
(Its) being established by valid cognition is indeed admitted.

sanskrit: prajñāvān prerakastasya yaḥ sa vijñeya īśvaraḥ || 15 ||
translation: He who, possessed of intelligence, is the impeller of that one — he is to be known as the Lord.

sanskrit: tasyāpi kartṛtā naiva caṇḍi tasyai namo'stu te || 15 || iti |
translation: Of him too there is no agency at all. O Caṇḍī, homage to you.
(That) from whose surge (of power) it acts, by day and by night (at all times).
It acts for the making of the world from Māyā, characterized by capacity — thus, (there is) no other Lord.
In the (case of the) surge, the cause of that is none other than Maheśvara.

sanskrit: ato'nyathānupapattyā jñānātiśayayuktaḥ parameśvara evodrede tasyāḥ kāraṇam || 17 ||
translation: Therefore, by the impossibility of (it being) otherwise, the Supreme Lord, endowed with an excess of knowledge, is the cause of that (activity of māyā) in the surge.

sanskrit: prakalpita evāstu | tarhi sarvajñatvādidharmikā prakṛtireveśvara iti vedāntavidaḥ ||
translation: Let it be imagined (so). Then, (say) the knowers of Vedānta: prakṛti itself, possessed of properties such as omniscience, is the Lord.
But from the supreme Self, Maheśa, possessed of the powers of seeing and acting, ...
If another world-lord were to arise from that, what fruit (would there be)?
If the origination of the world of conscious and unconscious (things) were from the Self, then he too, indeed, (would be a material cause, hence insentient).
Because the specific forms of effects — pots etc. produced from gold, clay, etc. — are established (each as arising from its own cause).
(Two) contradictory properties, situated at one time, having come to a single substratum (are said to be contradictory).

sanskrit: kenacinnetyucyate, yadyevaṃ sabhāgatve sati ghaṭādivat kāryatvāt paramakāraṇatvāyogaḥ ||
translation: 'By something (else)' — thus it is said. If (it is) so, then, being in the same class (as effects), like a pot, because of being an effect, supreme cause-hood is impossible.
Because of (being) a material cause, like clay, the Supreme Self is not conscious.
Because of (its) being a cause. Or, if (it is) conscious, then (it has) no material-cause-hood — thus.
This was said by us at length in the commentary on the Paramokṣanirāsakārikā; it is to be determined there.
If the Supreme Self had the property of producing the insentient, like clay etc., (it would be insentient).
For the accomplishment of its own effect, like clay, it must be admitted (to be) impelled by an intelligent agent.
Therefore the enjoyer (is) the seed of the world, and Maheśa (is) possessed of power.

sanskrit: supte'pi vikṛtijāte tritayaṃ jāgarti tattvānām || (ślo0 3) ityupādānakāraṇādanyaḥ
translation: Even when the modification-born (world) is asleep, the triad of the tattvas stays awake — (as the verse, śl. 3, says); thus (the world-maker is) other than the material cause.
The power of the Trident-bearer, whose form is all knowledge and action, is one alone.

sanskrit: na vāstavo jñānakriyāśaktyorbhedaḥ, api tu kalpita eva || 25 ||
translation: The distinction between the powers of knowledge and action is not real; rather, it is imagined only.
The production of many effects by the power of action is established and uncontradicted — thus, its (apparent) distinction too is imagined, because of the difference of operations.
With (his) action, Maheśvara restrains the impure selves.
And he impels the regulated ones according to the maturation of karma.

sanskrit: tatasteṣāṃ ca nunnānāṃ patyā saṃjāyate bhṛśam || 27 ||
translation: Then, of those impelled ones, (the effect) arises abundantly through the Lord.
The production of the fitness for the relation of effect and cause — this alone is called the Lord's impulsion.
In the infinite Self, the seat of authority over the pure and the impure, (called) Vidyeśa, ...

sanskrit: jagatkaroti patiḥ | yacchūyate - vidyārājādhirājeśo jagad bhrāmayatīcchayā iti || 28 ||
translation: The Lord makes the world. As is recited: 'The Lord of the supreme kings of knowledge whirls the world by his will.'
Having joined the world to those selves possessed of longing, ...
The Lord makes the abiding (state of the world) take the form of sādhana (the means of attainment).
At the end of the abiding, he too, for the sake of rest, (makes them) run through saṃsāra.
Then the Blessed One performs the total reabsorption (of the world).
The operations characterized as preservation of abiding, taking(-back), and non-existence are declared (to be) distinct.
By initiation alone he liberates the bound souls.

sanskrit: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca svato'bhinnāpi sā tridhā || 32 ||
translation: Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī — that (power), though undivided in itself, is threefold by nature.

sanskrit: sarvajñānakriyārūpā śaktirekaiva śūlinaḥ (mo0 25 ) iti na doṣaḥ kaścit || 32 ||
translation: 'The power of the Trident-bearer, whose form is all knowledge and action, is one alone' (Mokṣakārikā 25) — thus, there is no fault at all.
Thus, in this way, the all-agency of the God of gods has been declared.
The establishment of omniscience — this was said before.
But (the effect is) endowed with material causes, efficient causes, and fruit.
But (the agent/cause is) endowed with material causes, efficient causes, and fruit.
One endowed with unstained knowledge of the three times is indeed inferred (as such) — thus, omniscience is established.
Thus, because of (its) effecting all objects, the power in the Self is two-formed.

sanskrit: yayā yukto maheśānaḥ sarvaṃ vetti karoti ca || 37 ||
translation: Endowed with which, Maheśāna knows everything and does everything.
Since a body is figuratively attributed (to him), Śiva is called 'with parts' (sakala).
He is not connected with a body of kalās; that one (the bound soul) is connected (with it), as the paśu (is).
Because, unlike the paśu, there is no body consisting of kalā etc. (for him), the Blessed One is 'without parts' (niṣkala) — this was said before.

sanskrit: nanvasya niṣkalatve tu na jñānaṃ nāpi kartṛtā || 39 ||
translation: But (objection:) if he is without parts, then surely there is no knowledge for him, nor agency.
(Then there would be) the absence of knowledge etc.
For the manifestation of consciousness, (knowledge) depends on union with kalā, when (that kalā is) duly fixed.
(Knowledge and action are) dependent on a manifestor — thus, always, in every matter.
Now (objection:) because of (this) non-knowing, the Lord's seeing and acting, like the paśu's, (would be) dependent on kalā etc. as manifestor.
Then he would become a bound soul.
Because of (his) connection with kalā etc., the Lord, like Devadatta etc., would (unwarrantedly) turn out to be a bound soul.
Thus (there is) infinite regress.

sanskrit: kalāḥ sṛṣṭvāpi tadyuktaḥ kāryakṛd yadyasau tataḥ || 42 ||
translation: If, even after creating the kalās, that one, endowed with them, (is) the effect-maker — then ...
'He makes (the world)' — thus it is said.

sanskrit: karotīti kiṃ tasya kalādiśarīra-kalpanayetyevamādivistareṇa nareśvaraparīkṣāyāṃ varṇitamiti ||
translation: 'He makes' — what (need) of imagining a body of kalās for him? In this way and at length it is described in the Nareśvaraparīkṣā.
Therefore, enough of this digression; (the Lord is) the accomplisher of enjoyment and liberation.
(He is) always to be worshipped, none other — thus is declared enjoyment together with its means.
(Mokṣa is) the cutting off of the bonds beginning with mala; (it is) the arising of all knowledge and action.
Because the bound self is (what is) liberated, it is held to be the object (karman) of liberation.

sanskrit: puṃso lopo'sau na svayaṃ veda || yata ityevaṃ viśiṣṭo'viśiṣṭo vā sarvaścātra mokṣaḥ
translation: 'The self's destruction — he does not himself know it.' Since (that is so), thus — whether qualified or unqualified — everything here (counts as) liberation.
It was promised: its means (is) the next treatise.
For let liberation be intrinsic to the self, like enjoyment; then the person (would be ...).
From the attainment of the form of omniscience etc., liberation is indeed effected by oneself — not effected by the Lord.
The ignorance born of the cognition of non-discrimination ceases.
By the cessation of its own cause alone would that cease — not otherwise.
Now, if that entity were a property of the self, then in (its) nothingness that would cease.
If (it is) something to be removed, (it is) not a property of the self; that (removal) (would be) the stopping of the beginningless (ignorance).
